official.deadline_note: The call for applications was open until 27 February 2026, 3:00:00 p.m. official time in Poland; submission is made by the host institution via the NAWA IT system. Results were scheduled by 31 July 2026 and the evaluation was concluded on 29 July 2026.
official.application_cycle: Pilot call No. 42/2025 of 12 November 2025; programme implementation period 1 September 2026 - 31 March 2032
official.status_note: The first (pilot) call, announced 12 November 2025 as Call No. 42/2025, closed on 27 February 2026. NAWA states the evaluation process was concluded on 29 July 2026 and has published the list of applications approved for funding (10 projects). The programme implementation period runs from 1 September 2026 to 31 March 2032. No new call had been announced as of the verification date.
official.funding_period: per year (maximum, full-time; Junior Fellow track)
benefits: Full-time employment contract for the Junior Fellow/Senior Fellow at a Polish university or research institute for 2-4 years

Remuneration for the Principal Investigator of up to PLN 240,000 per year (Junior Fellow track) or PLN 330,000 per year (Senior Fellow track) in the case of full-time employment, amounts including employer costs
Remuneration for members of the Project Group of up to PLN 160,000 per year in total (Junior Fellow track) or PLN 250,000 per year in total (Senior Fellow track)
Remuneration for the Inviting Person of up to PLN 14,400 per year
Maximum project funding of PLN 1,243,200 in the Junior Fellow track and PLN 2,377,600 in the Senior Fellow track
Optional NCN Research Component of up to PLN 400,000 (basic research) or NCBR Applied Research Component of up to PLN 400,000 (industrial research and development work)
Call budget of PLN 17 million from NAWA, financed from national funds
eligibility: Junior Fellow track: citizenship other than Polish; doctoral degree obtained no earlier than 7 years before submitting the application; at least 12 months of work as a researcher during the last 24 months (from the date of the Call announcement) in a centre of a high level of scientific excellence outside Poland ranked 1 to 200 in the Shanghai Ranking (ARWU 2025), QS World University Rankings or THE World University Rankings 2025; outstanding scientific achievements of international recognition

Senior Fellow track: citizenship other than Polish; at least a doctoral degree; at least 36 months of work as a researcher during the last 48 months in a top-200 centre outside Poland; outstanding scientific achievements of international recognition; proven experience in managing a research team or managing at least one research project selected in a competition (excluding individual scholarships and projects organised by the Principal Investigator's employer)
The programme is open to all fields of science; representatives of the arts may participate provided the planned activities are of a scientific nature

Eligible applicants are the host institutions - entities referred to in art. 7 par. 1 points 1, 2 and 4-7 of the Act of 20 July 2018 (Law on Higher Education and Science) - that employ the Principal Investigator
Citizens of the Russian Federation, and institutions and other entities based in the territory of the Russian Federation, are excluded from participation
A Principal Investigator may appear in only one application submitted in the call; a Host Institution may submit multiple applications, each with a different Principal Investigator
requirements: The application must be completed in English; applications prepared in Polish will be disregarded
Applications are submitted only in electronic form via the Agency's IT system at https://programs.nawa.gov.pl

The host institution undertakes to conclude an employment contract with the Principal Investigator, employ members of the Project Group, provide office and laboratory space, research equipment and access to research infrastructure, ensure administrative and financial support, support future grant applications, and support obtaining required consents and permits
The Principal Investigator is expected to be fully relocated to Poland and employed full-time, with the centre of personal and economic interests in Poland
The Principal Investigator must not undertake employment in Poland between submitting the application and receiving the Director's decision or the planned date of announcement of results
Creation of a Project Group is mandatory
documents: Power of attorney for the person submitting the application to represent the Applicant - in Polish; template provided in the appendix to the Call
A scan of the document confirming that the Principal Investigator is a PhD holder - in the original language
Invitation of the Principal Investigator by the Host institution, signed by the Inviting Person - in English (template attached to the Call)

A copy of documents confirming that the Principal Investigator worked as a researcher outside Poland under the conditions specified in the Call (a certificate from the HR department or from a person representing the employer's institution, with the name of the position and the period of employment) - in English
3-5 most relevant publications of the Principal Investigator
Attachments in electronic form: a scan of a document with a handwritten signature or a document with a qualified electronic signature
selection_criteria: Formal assessment of completeness and compliance with the Call Announcement, followed by merit-based assessment under the Regulations for Institutional Programmes for Researchers
Initial assessment by the Team of Experts (max 15 points): the Principal Investigator's scientific or academic career and scientific achievements to date

Assessment by two External Reviewers (average ratings, max 40 points): PI achievements (10), justification for the selection of the Host institution (10), scientific or technological quality of the Project (10), impact of the Project on the development of science (10)
Final assessment by the Team of Experts (max 45 points), which may include online interviews with candidates for Principal Investigator to discuss research plans; maximum total 100 points
coverage: Funding under the Programme includes remuneration for the Principal Investigator, Project Group members, and the Inviting Person; remuneration amounts include employer costs
Maximum total project funding of PLN 1,243,200 (Junior Fellow track) and PLN 2,377,600 (Senior Fellow track), settled on the basis of actual expenses incurred
The host institution provides conditions for research: office and laboratory space, research equipment, access to infrastructure for research and teaching, administrative and financial support

Optional additional component of up to PLN 400,000 from the National Science Centre (NCN) for basic research or up to PLN 400,000 from the National Centre for Research and Development (NCBR) for applied research
The programme is financed from national funds with a call budget of PLN 17 million; the call documentation does not publish coverage of travel, relocation or visa costs
application_method: Electronic submission only, via the Agency's IT system: https://programs.nawa.gov.pl
Application prepared in English in line with Call for Applications No. 42/2025 of 12 November 2025; the application form template is published with the call
The host institution submits the application naming a single Principal Investigator; the most recently submitted application is prioritised if a PI appears in several
official.application_route: A Polish host institution applies electronically at programs.nawa.gov.pl in English; the researcher must first secure a host institution and an Inviting Person (NAWA points to researchinpoland.org as the recommended platform for identifying a supervisor or host).
official.study_mode: full-time (the Principal Investigator must be employed full-time at the host institution in Poland)
official.citizenship_residency: The Principal Investigator must be of citizenship other than Polish and must fully relocate to Poland, with the centre of personal and economic interests in Poland; citizens of the Russian Federation and Russia-based institutions and entities are excluded from participation
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the programme is designed to attract foreign researchers: the Principal Investigator must be a non-Polish citizen currently working at a top-200 ranked centre outside Poland
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Open to all fields of science; representatives of the arts may participate provided the planned activities are of a scientific nature. The host must be an eligible Polish higher education and science institution (entities referred to in art. 7 par. 1 points 1, 2 and 4-7 of the Act of 20 July 2018)
official.research_requirement: The application must present a research plan; the Principal Investigator must demonstrate outstanding scientific achievements of international recognition (Senior Fellow track also requires experience managing a research team or a competitively selected research project); 3-5 most relevant publications are a required attachment
official.duration: Junior Fellow track: no less than 24 and no longer than 36 months; Senior Fellow track: no less than 36 and no longer than 48 months (project start between 1 September 2026 and 1 April 2027; extension of up to 12 months possible without increased funding). Programme implementation period: 1 September 2026 - 31 March 2032
official.description: TOP200 NAWA is an initiative of the Polish National Agency for Academic Exchange aimed at supporting transnational science cooperation and fostering excellent research in Poland by inviting scientists with outstanding scientific achievements from centres ranked 1 to 200 in the Shanghai, QS or THE global rankings. It provides foreign researchers the opportunity to work in Poland for 2-4 years and establish their own project groups through two tracks - Junior Fellow and Senior Fellow - with the host institution employing the Principal Investigator and receiving NAWA funding for salaries and project costs.
official.program_type: Research employment programme (fellowship tracks) hosted by Polish universities and research institutes
official.english_requirement: The application must be completed in English; applications prepared in Polish will be disregarded. The invitation of the Principal Investigator and the certificates confirming research work outside Poland must be in English. No IELTS/TOEFL or other formal English test score is published

not_confirmed: Travel, relocation and visa costs - the official call documentation does not mention any coverage of these
Tuition fees or tuition coverage - not applicable/published, as the programme is research employment rather than a degree programme
Whether and when a follow-up call will be announced after the pilot round - no new call was announced as of the verification date
Any formal English language test score (IELTS/TOEFL) - only the English-language application rule is published
verification.notes: Amounts, caps, deadline, eligibility, documents and assessment were taken from the official Call for Applications No. 42/2025 PDF on nawa.gov.pl and the TOP200 NAWA programme pages; status confirmed on the official call-results page (evaluation concluded 29 July 2026, 10 projects approved).

applicant_utility.summary: You cannot apply directly: a Polish host institution must be willing to employ you full-time and submit the application for you through programs.nawa.gov.pl, so the practical first step is securing a host and an Inviting Person. Your eligibility hinges on documented research employment - at least 12 of the last 24 months (Junior Fellow) or 36 of the last 48 months (Senior Fellow) - at a university ranked in the global top 200 outside Poland. The pilot round closed on 27 February 2026 and funded 10 fellows, so the immediate opportunity depends on NAWA announcing a new call.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Internationally mobile researchers with a recent or established doctorate who are currently working at a top-200 ranked university abroad and can persuade a Polish institution to host and employ them.
application_readiness_checklist: Secure a host institution that confirms it will employ you full-time and can provide lab/office space and administrative support
Get an Inviting Person (a researcher at the host) to sign the English invitation template from the call
Obtain an HR or employer certificate stating your position title and exact employment periods abroad, in English
Prepare your PhD certificate scan in its original language and select your 3-5 most relevant publications
Have the host's authorised signatory arrange the Polish-language power of attorney on the NAWA template
Check that you will not be employed in Poland between submission and the results announcement, and that your centre of personal and economic interests can move to Poland
common_rejection_risks: Weak or ambiguous evidence of the required 12/36 months of research employment at a top-200 institution - the certificate must name the position and period
The same Principal Investigator appearing in more than one application, which triggers prioritisation of only the latest submission
A host institution that cannot realistically commit to full-time employment and the promised research infrastructure
Failing to demonstrate achievements of international recognition at your career stage, or (Senior track) no proof of having led a team or won a competitive project
Formal rejection at a later assessment stage for incomplete attachments despite a strong research plan
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Relocation to Poland, residence/visa formalities and personal living costs before the employment contract starts are not funded by the programme; the call publishes no travel or relocation allowance. Any project start-date postponement or extension of up to 12 months comes without increased funding, so gaps between contracts are self-funded.
document_audit: The power of attorney must be in Polish and follow the template in the call appendix - a foreign-language or generic letter will not do
The invitation must be signed personally by the Inviting Person, a researcher at the host institution, not by an administrative office alone
The employment-abroad certificate must state the exact position name and the period of employment; a bare reference letter without dates is a common gap
The PhD document scan stays in its original language - no translation is required by the call, but an unclear scan causes formal queries
All attachments must be scans with handwritten signatures or bear a qualified electronic signature
alerts: Polish citizens cannot be the Principal Investigator, and citizens of the Russian Federation (and Russia-based entities) are excluded from the programme
Taking up any paid employment in Poland before the results are announced disqualifies the application
The PI salary figures are annual maximum caps including employer costs, not guaranteed amounts - the actual salary is negotiated with the host within that cap
After the pilot round closed in February 2026, no new call had been announced as of 10 October 2026; watch the NAWA TOP200 pages and the programme schedule before planning an application
Only one application per Principal Investigator is allowed, and the most recent submission is the one assessed if duplicates exist
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: The host institution's authorised person submits the English-language application electronically at programs.nawa.gov.pl before the call deadline; NAWA then runs a formal completeness check, a Team of Experts initial assessment, two external reviews and a final expert stage that may include an online interview, with results announced by the date given in the call.
